decisions.summary: An interview transcript and an independently created audio recording of the same 2024-02-02 interview both contain Mayor Imani stating that Eastport unemployment fell by 20 percent between 2022 and 2023, so the attribution claim is supported even though the embedded statistic itself was not verified.

evidence.finding: Interview transcript dated 2024-02-02 records Mayor Imani saying Eastport unemployment fell by 20 percent between 2022 and 2023; no dataset provided.
Reporter B independently audio-recorded the interview on 2024-02-02; the recording contains the same Imani statement; Reporter B did not verify the statistic.

gaps: The embedded statistic (20 percent fall) is not verified in this packet; only the act of saying it is established.

decisions.summary: Two declared-independent citywide 2023 Westport delivery measurements using the same order-confirmed-to-door-received metric yield medians of 28 minutes and 34 minutes on opposite sides of the 30-minute threshold, and the supplied record states the discrepancy is unresolved.

evidence.finding: Lab A independently sampled completed citywide Westport deliveries across calendar 2023 (order-confirmed to door-received, raw sample reviewed by Lab A) and estimates a median of 28 minutes.

Lab B independently collected its own citywide 2023 sample (same metric), estimates a median of 34 minutes, states it did not use Lab A's observations or calculations, and notes the discrepancy has not been resolved.

gaps: The methodological or sampling cause of the 28 vs 34 minute discrepancy is unidentified and remains unresolved.
contradictions: Lab A's 28-minute median vs Lab B's 34-minute median for the same population-year metric.

ledger.component: In 2023, the independently measured median delivery time in Westport was less than 30 minutes.
ledger.question: Do independent measurements of the 2023 Westport citywide median delivery time agree it was below 30 minutes?
ledger.evidentiary_origin: W1: Lab A's own reviewed sample and calculation; W2: Lab B's independently collected sample, explicitly not using Lab A's observations or calculations
ledger.unresolved_material_question: Which estimate (28 or 34 minutes) better reflects the true 2023 median; the discrepancy is stated as unresolved in W2.

decisions.summary: The causal claim rests solely on the vendor's own unadjusted before/after comparison, which the vendor concedes did not control for traffic volume, construction, seasonality or other changes, and the Bulletin merely repeats those figures without independent verification.

evidence.finding: Vendor press release attributes a 15 percent reduction in junction delays vs 2023 to its signal system, but states it did not adjust for traffic volume, construction, seasonality or other changes.
The Southport Bulletin article repeats the vendor press release figures and explicitly did not collect or independently verify any measurements.

gaps: No independent or official measurement of junction delays in 2023 and 2024 exists in the packet.
No data on installation date, traffic volume, roadworks or seasonality confounders for 2023–2024.
No study or report attributes the delay change specifically to the signal system versus alternative explanations.

ledger.component: In 2024, Southport's new signal system caused a 15 percent reduction in junction delays compared with 2023.
ledger.question: Is there evidence the signal system causally caused a 15 percent reduction in junction delays vs 2023?
ledger.event_or_data_date: Publication dates 2024-06-01 and 2024-06-02; comparison period 2023 vs 2024; measurement collection dates not established
ledger.evidentiary_origin: S1: vendor's own before/after observation, self-declared unadjusted; S2: repetition of the vendor's figures with no independent verification
ledger.unresolved_material_question: Whether alternative explanations (volume, construction, seasonality) account for any observed change; vendor admits no adjustment.

decisions.summary: For the 2020-02-19 reference date, Forbes-based Bloomberg net worth of $64.2 billion exceeds the combined wealth of the bottom 38 percent of US households (~125.7 million people) both as computed from the 2019 Survey of Consumer Finances ($11.4B, Bruenig derivation) and in PolitiFact's independent replication (~$6B), so the comparison holds under either wealth figure; Bloomberg's status as former New York mayor is corroborated by PolitiFact.

evidence.finding: Bloomberg's net worth is $64.2 billion according to Forbes, making him the eighth wealthiest person in America.

Per the latest Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances, the bottom 38 percent of households (~125.7 million people at 2.63 members per household) have a collective net worth of $11.4 billion, so Bloomberg owns nearly six times that wealth; author notes even the 125 million figure may understate.

PolitiFact had an experienced data analyst (Gross, University of Michigan) replicate Bruenig's math independently; Gross found the bottom 38% held about $6 billion rather than $11.4 billion, but this was still enough to verify that Bloomberg had more wealth than the bottom 38% of households combined.
PolitiFact confirms Sanders said the statement at the Feb. 19 Las Vegas debate and describes Bloomberg as 'the former mayor of New York'.
Jacobin presents the same SCF basis (bottom 38%, $11.4B) and same Forbes $64.2B figure; presentation parallels S1 closely, indicating shared derivation rather than independent verification.
Common Dreams reports only Sanders's own use of the statistic at the debate; it is a quoting of the claim, not an independent check of the wealth math.

gaps: The bottom-125-million population is an author-derived approximation (38% of households × 2.63 members); the exact count of people could differ.
Exact dating of the Forbes net worth estimate is not established in the supplied passages beyond the 2020-02-19 publication context.
A materially different bottom-38% wealth estimate ($6B per Gross vs $11.4B per Bruenig) exists, though it does not change the outcome of the comparison.
contradictions: Gross's replication put bottom-38% combined wealth at about $6 billion versus Bruenig's $11.4 billion (S2 P2); both figures remain far below Bloomberg's $64.2 billion, so the contradiction is immaterial to the verdict.
